Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr ibn Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Abu Salamah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: the line that the Arabs would draw in the earth.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr, meaning Ibn 'Ayyash, said: the khatt (line) is the 'iyafah (augury by birds and marks).

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: or some special knowledge.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: or special knowledge.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: that is, special knowledge.

* Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from al-Husayn, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: special knowledge.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: or knowledge that you extract and bring forth.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: athara is something they extract by natural disposition (fitrah).

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: or do you transmit that as knowledge from someone of those before you?

Mention of those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: someone who transmits knowledge.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: or by a clear proof of the matter.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: it means: by a clear proof of the matter.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: by a remnant of knowledge.

Mention of those who said this:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr, meaning Ibn 'Ayyash, was asked about ﴿athara min 'ilm﴾, and he said: a remnant of knowledge.

"And a she-camel with a remnant [of fat], which ate upon it a pasture, desolate in its hillock."

[This is a verse from an ode of al-Ra'i, in which he praised Sa'd ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Attab ibn Usayd; its count is fifty-seven verses. ... (editorial footnote on the verse, lexical notes, and attribution to al-Shammakh)]

That is: and a she-camel possessing a remnant of fat. As for one who reads ﴿or athrah﴾, he took it to be from the root "athar" (trace), as is said: qatrah and ghabrah. It has been mentioned of some of them that he read ﴿or athrah﴾ with a sukun on the tha', like al-rajfah and al-khatfah. When this is interpreted, as we have said, as a remnant of knowledge, it is permissible that this remnant of knowledge be of the knowledge of the line, or of knowledge extracted from the books of the earlier people, or of special knowledge they were preferred with. It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a report regarding this, that he interpreted it to mean the line, which we shall mention, if Allah the Exalted wills. The meaning of the speech is therefore: Bring me, O people, a Book before this Book, by establishing what I have asked you to establish, the proof for your claim concerning what you ascribe to your gods, or a remnant of knowledge by which you may arrive at knowledge of the soundness of what you say about that, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your claim that they possess what you assert, for a claim that has no proof with it does not avail the claimant anything.

For if that were established for them, then a partnership in the blessings in which you live would be established for them, and thanks would be due to them from you, and service would be owed to them by you, since none can create that except Allah.

* *

As for His words ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾:

The reciters differed in the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq read it ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾ with an alif (أَثَارَةٍ), meaning: or bring me a remnant of knowledge. It is narrated from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he read it "أَوْ أَثَرَةٍ مِنْ عِلْمٍ" (or a preference of knowledge), meaning: or a special knowledge that you have been given and preferred with over others. The reading I do not permit other than is ﴿أَثَارَةٍ﴾ with the alif, due to the consensus of the reciters of the major cities upon it.

The people of interpretation differed concerning its meaning. Some said: its meaning is: or bring me knowledge that your gods created something of the earth, and that they have a share in the heavens, from the line that you draw in the earth, for you, the community of the Arabs, are people of augury, divination and soothsaying.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr ibn Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Abu Salamah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: the line that the Arabs would draw in the earth.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr, meaning Ibn 'Ayyash, said: the khatt (line) is the 'iyafah (augury by birds and marks).

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: or some special knowledge.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: or special knowledge.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: that is, special knowledge.

* Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from al-Husayn, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: special knowledge.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: or knowledge that you extract and bring forth.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: athara is something they extract by natural disposition (fitrah).

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: or do you transmit that as knowledge from someone of those before you?

Mention of those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: someone who transmits knowledge.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: or by a clear proof of the matter.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿or some trace of knowledge﴾, he said: it means: by a clear proof of the matter.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: by a remnant of knowledge.

Mention of those who said this:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr, meaning Ibn 'Ayyash, was asked about ﴿athara min 'ilm﴾, and he said: a remnant of knowledge.

The most correct of these opinions in the view of truth is the statement of the one who said: al-athara is the remnant of knowledge, because that is the well-known meaning in the speech of the Arabs, and it is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: athara al-shay' athara, like samija samaja and qabuha qabaha, as the camel-herd said:

"And a she-camel with a remnant [of fat], which ate upon it a pasture, desolate in its hillock."

[This is a verse from an ode of al-Ra'i, in which he praised Sa'd ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Attab ibn Usayd; its count is fifty-seven verses. ... (editorial footnote on the verse, lexical notes, and attribution to al-Shammakh)]

That is: and a she-camel possessing a remnant of fat. As for one who reads ﴿or athrah﴾, he took it to be from the root "athar" (trace), as is said: qatrah and ghabrah. It has been mentioned of some of them that he read ﴿or athrah﴾ with a sukun on the tha', like al-rajfah and al-khatfah. When this is interpreted, as we have said, as a remnant of knowledge, it is permissible that this remnant of knowledge be of the knowledge of the line, or of knowledge extracted from the books of the earlier people, or of special knowledge they were preferred with. It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a report regarding this, that he interpreted it to mean the line, which we shall mention, if Allah the Exalted wills. The meaning of the speech is therefore: Bring me, O people, a Book before this Book, by establishing what I have asked you to establish, the proof for your claim concerning what you ascribe to your gods, or a remnant of knowledge by which you may arrive at knowledge of the soundness of what you say about that, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your claim that they possess what you assert, for a claim that has no proof with it does not avail the claimant anything.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are, of their supplication, unaware (5)﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And what servant is more astray than a servant who calls upon gods other than Allah, which will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection? That is: they will never answer his supplication, because they are stone, or wood, or the like.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they are, of their supplication, unaware﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Their gods whom they call upon are unaware of their supplication to them, because they do not hear, do not speak, and do not understand. He only meant by describing them as unaware the comparison of them to a heedless person who is unaware of what is said to him, since they do not understand anything of what is said to them, just as one who is unaware of a thing does not understand what he is unaware of. This is in fact a rebuke from Allah to these polytheists for their bad judgment and the ugliness of their choice in worshipping one who understands nothing and comprehends nothing, and for their abandoning the worship of Him who is the source of all the blessings they have, and to whom they cry for help when needs and calamities befall them.

It has been said: "one who will not respond to him" refers to the gods, which are inanimate, but is expressed in the manner of reference to the sons of Adam, who possess choice and discernment, since its worshippers had likened them to kings and rulers who are served by those who attend upon them, so the speech about them proceeded in the manner that was customary among them.

He, the Exalted, says: when the people are gathered on the Day of Resurrection for the standing of reckoning, those deities they used to call upon in the world will be enemies to them, because they will disown them. ﴿And they will be disbelievers in their worship﴾: He, the Exalted, says: their deities whom they worshipped in the world will deny their worship, because they will say on the Day of Resurrection, "We did not order them to worship us, and we were not aware of their worshipping us. He, the Exalted, says: when these polytheists from your people, who associate others with God, are recited Our verses, meaning Our proofs which We have established against them in what We sent down in Our Book upon Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿as clear evidences﴾, meaning manifest and luminous. ﴿Those who disbelieved say of the truth when it has come to them﴾: He, the Exalted, says: those who denied the Oneness of God and denied His Messenger said of the truth, when it came to them from God, and so He sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ) ﴿This is obvious magic﴾, meaning they mean this Qur'an is a deception that deceives us, and it captures the hearts of those who hear it like the working of magic. ﴿Obvious﴾: it says, it makes clear to whoever contemplates it among those who hear it that it is obvious magic.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿what you spread about in it﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 9:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a plain warner.﴾ (9)

God, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people from Quraysh: ﴿I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾, meaning: I am not the first of the messengers of God whom He has sent to His creatures. Messengers came before me, and many messengers were sent to nations before you. It is said of this: "He is bid' (a novelty) in this matter" and "badi' (unprecedented) in it," when he is the first in it. Among the uses of bid' is the verse of 'Adi ibn Zayd:

"So I am not a novelty among the events that befall men, who perished after misery and happiness."[[The line is by 'Adi ibn Zayd (Poets of Christianity, p. 465), and its version there is: "So I am not one to fear the events that befall men, who perished after misery and happiness." There is no evidence for this version in it. The author cited it to show that it is said: "He is bid' in this matter," in the sense that "I was not the first of people in it." And God's saying, "Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers," means: I was not the first to be sent; many messengers were sent before me.]]

And among the uses of badi' is the verse of al-Ahwas:

"She boasted and claimed kinship, so I said: Look at me. Your ignorance that you came with is not unprecedented."[[Al-Ahwas says: she boasted over me and claimed kinship with her fathers. I said: Enough; your ignorance toward me is neither unprecedented nor strange, for I have known the like of it from women like you. The line is among the evidences of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (fol. 222, 1), where he cites it to show that badi' has the meaning of bid', in his explanation of God's saying, "Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers."]]

It means "first," and it is said: "He is a bid' of a people, abdad'."

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾: he means, I am not the first of the messengers.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾: he said: he means, I am not the first messenger sent.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾: he said: I am not the first of them.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Abu Hubayrah, who said: I asked Qatadah about ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾, and he said: That is, messengers came before me.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾: he means, messengers had come before me.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿a novelty among the messengers﴾: he said: messengers had come before him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾

The people of interpretation differed about its interpretation. Some of them said: it refers to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and it was said to him: Say to those who believe in you: I do not know what will be done with me or with you on the Day of Resurrection, or where we will end up there. They said: then God made clear to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and to the believers in him their state in the Hereafter, and it was said to him: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that God may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾, and He said: ﴿that He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and remove from them their misdeeds﴾.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾: then God revealed after this ﴿that God may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said: In Ha-Mim al-Ahqaf, ﴿and I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a plain warner﴾ was abrogated by the verse in Surah al-Fath, ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that God may forgive you﴾ ... the verse. The Prophet of God (ﷺ) went out when this verse was revealed and gave them the good news that his earlier and later sins had been forgiven. Some of the believers said to him: Congratulations to you, O Prophet of God; we know what will be done with you, so what will be done with us? Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed in Surah al-Ahzab, saying ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from God a great bounty﴾, and He said ﴿that He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and remove from them their misdeeds; and that is with God a great achievement, and that He may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women who think ill of God﴾ ... the verse, so God made clear what would be done with him and with them.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾: then he knew, or the Messenger of God (ﷺ) learned afterward, what would be done with him, saying ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that God may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾: he said: He made clear to him that his earlier and later sins had been forgiven.

Others said: rather, that is a command from God, Exalted is His praise, to His Prophet, upon whom be blessings and peace, to say it to the polytheists of his people, and to make known that he does not know how his affair and theirs will end in this world: whether his affair with them will lead to their killing him or expelling him from among them, or their believing in him and following him, or their affair ending in destruction, as the nations that denied their messengers before them were destroyed, or in their confirming him in what came to them from God.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾: he said: As for the Hereafter, God forbid; he knew he would be in Paradise when his covenant was taken among the messengers. Rather, he said: "I do not know what will be done with me or with you in this world: whether I will be expelled as the prophets before me were expelled, or killed as the prophets before me were killed; and I do not know what will be done with me or with you, whether my people will be the deniers, or my people the confirmers, or my people pelted with stones from the sky, or swallowed up by the earth." Then it was revealed to him: ﴿And when We said to you, indeed your Lord encompasses the people﴾, meaning: I have encompassed for you the Arabs so that they will not kill you, and he knew that he would not be killed.

Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, and sufficient is God as witness﴾, meaning: He bears witness for you by Himself that He will make your religion prevail over the religions. Then He said to him concerning his community: ﴿And God would not punish them while you are among them, and God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. Thus God informed him what He would do with him and what He would do with his community.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: I do not know what will be obligated upon me and upon you, or what judgment will be sent down; it does not mean "I do not know what will be done with me or with you tomorrow in the return, of God's reward for those who obey Him, or His punishment for those who deny Him."

Others said: He was only commanded to say this concerning a matter he was awaiting from God, Mighty and Majestic, other than reward and punishment.

The most correct of these sayings, and the one most consistent with what the revelation indicates, is the saying of al-Hasan al-Basri, which Abu Bakr al-Hudhali transmitted from him.

We say this because the address from the beginning of this surah up to this verse, and the report, came from God, Mighty and Majestic, as address to the polytheists and report about them, and as rebuke to them, and as God's argument, Exalted is His mention, for His Prophet (ﷺ) against them.

Given that this is so, it is known that this verse also follows the path of what precedes and follows it, in that it is an argument against them, a rebuke to them, or a report about them. Given that, it is impossible to say to the Prophet (ﷺ): Say to the polytheists: I do not know what will be done with me or with you in the Hereafter, while the verses of God's Book in its revelation and its inspiration to him are consecutive that the polytheists abide forever in the Fire and the believers in Him abide in gardens blessed, and with that He frightens them at times and entices them at others. If he had said that to them, they would have said to him: Then on what basis should we follow you, while you do not know what state you will be in tomorrow on the Day of Resurrection, whether in ease and rest or in hardship and punishment? Our following you, if we follow you, and our confirming what you call us to, is out of desire for a blessing and honor we hope for, or fear of a punishment and torment we flee from. But it is as al-Hasan said. Then God made clear to His Prophet (ﷺ) what He would do with him, and with those among his people and others who denied what he brought.

* *

As for His saying ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾

God, Mighty and Majestic, says: Say to them: I do not follow, in what I command you and in what I do, anything but the revelation of God that He reveals to me. ﴿And I am only a plain warner﴾, meaning: I am only a warner to you, warning you of God's punishment for your disbelief in Him, plain: meaning, He has made clear to you His warning and made manifest to you His call to what contains your advice. He says: So likewise am I.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like and believes, while you are arrogant [...] Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [46:10].

Exalted is His remembrance says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who say of this Qur'an, when it came to them, that it is "clear magic": ﴿Have you considered?﴾ O people, ﴿if it is﴾ this Qur'an ﴿from Allah﴾, He sent it down to me, ﴿and you disbelieve in it﴾, meaning: and you deny it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like﴾:

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: and a witness from the Children of Israel, who is Musa ibn 'Imran (peace be upon him), testifies to its like, meaning to the like of the Qur'an. They said: the like of the Qur'an to which Musa testified as confirmation is the Torah.

Mention of those who said this:

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir, from Masruq, regarding this verse: ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like﴾, that he disputed by it with those who disbelieved among the people of Makkah: the Torah is like the Qur'an, and Musa is like Muhammad ﷺ.

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud was asked about His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it⦆ ... the verse. Dawud said: 'Amir said: Masruq said: "By Allah, it was not revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Salam; it was revealed only in Makkah, and 'Abd Allah did not embrace Islam except in Madinah, but it was a dispute which Muhammad ﷺ conducted with his people." He said: Then it was revealed: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like and believes, while you are arrogant﴾. He said: The Torah is like the Qur'an, and Musa is like Muhammad ﷺ; so they believed in the Torah and in their messenger, and you disbelieved.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, say: "People claim that the witness from the Children of Israel concerning its like is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, but 'Abd Allah ibn Salam embraced Islam only in Madinah; and Masruq has informed me that Ha Mim [the surahs beginning with them] was revealed only in Makkah, and it was only the argument of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his people." So He said: ﴿Have you considered? If it is from Allah﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like and believes﴾, meaning Musa and Muhammad, peace be upon them, concerning the Criterion (al-Furqan).

- Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "Some people claim that the witness concerning its like is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, and I know better about that. 'Abd Allah embraced Islam in Madinah, and Masruq has informed me that Ha Mim was revealed only in Makkah, and it was only the argument of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his people. So He said: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah﴾, meaning the Criterion, ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like﴾; so the like of the Torah is the Criterion. The Torah was testified to by Musa, and Muhammad (testifies) concerning the Criterion, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace."

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, regarding His saying ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah﴾ ... the verse. He said: The Islam of Ibn Salam was in Madinah, and this surah was revealed in Makkah; it was only a dispute between Muhammad, peace be upon him, and his people. So He said: (Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like), He said: the Torah is like the Criterion, and Musa is like Muhammad. "So he believed in it, and you were arrogant." Then He said: this man from the Children of Israel believed in his prophet and his book, and you were arrogant, so you denied your prophet and your book. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide﴾ ... up to His saying ﴿This is an ancient falsehood﴾.

Others said: by His saying ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like﴾ He meant 'Abd Allah ibn Salam. They said: the meaning of the speech is: and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to the like of this Qur'an, confirming it. They said: the like of the Qur'an is the Torah.

Mention of those who said this:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Tinnisi narrated to us, saying: I heard Malik ibn Anas narrate from Abu al-Nadr, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, who said: "I did not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to anyone walking on the earth that he is among the people of Paradise except to 'Abd Allah ibn Salam." He said: And concerning him was revealed: ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like﴾.

- al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sudai narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated to us, saying: Shu'ayb ibn Safwan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr narrated to us, that Muhammad ibn Yusuf ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Salam said: 'Abd Allah said: "There was revealed concerning me: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah﴾ ... up to His saying ﴿and believes, while you are arrogant﴾."

- 'Ali ibn Sa'd ibn Masruq al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Abu Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Ya'la narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from the nephew of 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salam said: "There was revealed concerning me: ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like and believes, while you are arrogant. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah﴾ ... the verse. He said: A man from the People of the Book had believed in Muhammad ﷺ, and he said: "We find him in the Torah." He was the best man among them and the most knowledgeable of them concerning the Book. The Jews disputed with the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Are you content that 'Abd Allah ibn Salam judge between me and you?" "Do you believe?" They said: Yes. So he sent for 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and said: "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah, written in the Torah and the Gospel?" He said: Yes. The Jews turned away, and 'Abd Allah ibn Salam embraced Islam. He is the one of whom Allah, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like and believes, while you are arrogant﴾, meaning: 'Abd Allah ibn Salam believed.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like﴾: 'Abd Allah ibn Salam.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah﴾ ... the verse. "We used to narrate that it is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, who believed in the Book of Allah, His messenger, and Islam, and he was one of the rabbis of the Jews."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like﴾: he said: It is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam.

- I was informed from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like﴾: the witness is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, and he was one of the rabbis, from the scholars of the Children of Israel. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to the Jews, and they came to him, and he asked them: "Do you know that I am the Messenger of Allah? You find me written with you in the Torah?" They said: We do not know what you are saying, and we are disbelievers in what you have brought. He said: "What sort of man is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam among you?" They said: Our scholar and our best. He said: "Are you content to have him judge between me and you?" They said: Yes. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, and he came, and he said: "What is your testimony, O son of Salam?" He said: I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that your book came from Allah. So he believed, and they disbelieved. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿so he believed, and you were arrogant﴾.

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: It reached me that when 'Abd Allah ibn Salam wished to embrace Islam, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews know that I am among their scholars, and that my father was among their scholars, and I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that they find you written with them in the Torah. Send for so-and-so and so-and-so, and whomever he named of the Jews, and hide me in your house, and ask them about me and about my father, for they will tell you that I am the most knowledgeable of them and that my father was among the most knowledgeable of them. I will go out to them, and I will testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that they find you written with them in the Torah, and that you were sent with guidance and the religion of truth." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did so; he hid him in his house and sent for the Jews, and they entered upon him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What about 'Abd Allah ibn Salam among you?" They said: The most knowledgeable of us in himself, and the most knowledgeable of us in his father. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you see, if he embraces Islam, will you embrace Islam?" They said: He will not embrace Islam, three times. Then he called him, and he came out and said: I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that they find you written with them in the Torah, and that you were sent with guidance and the religion of truth. The Jews said: "We did not fear you would do this, O 'Abd Allah ibn Salam." He said: So they went out as disbelievers, and Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning that: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like and believes, while you are arrogant﴾.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like and believes, while you are arrogant﴾: This is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, who testified that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his book are true, and it is true in the Torah; so he believed, and you were arrogant.

- Abu Shurahbil al-Himsi narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, saying: Safwan ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, from 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who said: The Prophet ﷺ set out, and I was with him, until we entered the synagogue of the Jews in Madinah on one of their festival days. They disliked our entering upon them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "O assembly of Jews, show me twelve men who testify that there is no god but Him, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and Allah will remove from every Jew under the sky the wrath with which He was angry." They were silent, and none of them answered him. He repeated it a third time, and none answered him. He turned away, and I was with him, until when we were about to leave, a man called from behind us: "Stay as you are, O Muhammad." He turned back, and that man said: "What sort of man do you know among you, O assembly of Jews?" They said: "By Allah, we do not know that there was among us a man more knowledgeable of the Book of Allah, nor more learned, than you, nor than your father, nor than your grandfather before your father." He said: "I testify by Allah that he is the Prophet ﷺ whom you find in the Torah and the Gospel." They said: "You lie." Then they returned his words and spoke evil to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "You have lied; we will not accept your word. As for before, you praised him with the good you praised; and as for now that he has believed, you have denied him and said what you said, so we will not accept your word." He said: We went out, three of us: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, myself, and 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, and Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah﴾ ... the verse.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that what Masruq said about its interpretation is closer to the apparent sense of the revelation, because His saying ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like﴾ comes in the context of rebuking the polytheists of Quraysh by Allah, exalted is His remembrance, and arguing against them on behalf of His Prophet ﷺ; this verse is similar to the verses before it, and no mention of the People of the Book or the Jews had preceded it, so that this verse would be directed toward them and revealed concerning them. Nor is there any indication, by meaning, that the speech has turned away from the stories of those previously mentioned. However, reports have come from a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that it was meant concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, and most of the people of interpretation hold this view; and they were more knowledgeable of the meanings of the Qur'an, of the occasion of its revelation, and of what was intended by it.

Thus the meaning of the speech, given that this is so, is: and 'Abd Allah ibn Salam testified, and he is the witness from the Children of Israel, to its like, meaning to the like of the Qur'an, which is the Torah; and that testimony is his attestation that Muhammad is written in the Torah as a prophet, which the Jews find written with them in the Torah, just as it is written in the Qur'an that he is a prophet.

* *

As for His saying ﴿so he believed, and you were arrogant﴾:

He says: 'Abd Allah ibn Salam believed and affirmed Muhammad ﷺ and what he brought from Allah, and you, O company of Jews, were arrogant toward belief in what 'Abd Allah ibn Salam believed in ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾. He says: Indeed Allah does not grant success in reaching the truth and guide onto the straight path the disbelieving people who wronged themselves by bringing upon themselves the wrath of Allah through their disbelief in Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 11:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it. And since they are not guided by it, they will say, 'This is an ancient falsehood.'"﴾

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: And those who denied the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) from among the Jews of the Children of Israel said to those who believed in him: If your affirmation of Muhammad in what he has brought you were good, you would not have preceded us in affirming it. This interpretation accords with the view of those who interpreted His saying, ﴿And a witness from the Children of Israel testified to its like﴾, as referring to ʿAbdullah ibn Salam. As for the interpretation of those who held that it refers to the polytheists of Quraysh, then the saying ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it"﴾ should be understood as referring to the polytheists of Quraysh. This is how Qatadah interpreted it, and in interpreting it that way he left aside the interpretation of His saying, ﴿And a witness from the Children of Israel testified to its like﴾, which he took as referring to ʿAbdullah ibn Salam.

Mention of the narrations on this:

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it"﴾, he said: Some people among the polytheists said: "We are more honourable, we are, we are; so if it were good, so-and-so and so-and-so would not have preceded us to it." But Allah singles out whom He wills for His mercy.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it"﴾, he said: Some speakers among the people said this, those who had been more honourable than them in the Jahiliyyah. They said: "By Allah, if this were good, the Banu so-and-so and the Banu so-and-so would not have preceded us to it." Allah singles out whom He wills for His mercy, and honours whom He wills with His mercy, blessed and exalted is He.

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿And since they are not guided by it﴾:

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: And since they did not perceive Muhammad and what he brought from Allah of guidance, so that they could be guided by it to the straight path, ﴿they will say, "This is an ancient falsehood."﴾ That is: they will say that this Qur'an which Muhammad (ﷺ) brought consists of ancient falsehoods, tales of the former peoples, just as He, mighty is His praise, reported of them: ﴿And they say, "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And before it was the Book of Musa, a guide and a mercy. And this is a Book confirming [it] in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who have wronged, and as good tidings for the doers of good.﴾ (46:12)**

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And before this Book was the Book of Musa, which is the Torah, as a guide (*imaman*) for the Children of Israel, whom they follow, and a mercy to them, which We sent down to them. The speech takes the form of a report about the Book without mentioning the complete report, being content with the indication of the speech on its completion. Its completion is: And before it was the Book of Musa, a guide and a mercy, which We sent down to him, and this is a Book which We sent down in the Arabic tongue.

Scholars differed in the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of this, and about the word that governs the accusative in ﴿in the Arabic tongue﴾ (*lisanan 'arabiyyan*). The grammarians (*ahl al-'arabiyya*) said: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: *lisanan* and *'arabiyyan* are in the accusative because they are a description of the Book, so they take the accusative as a circumstantial accusative (*hal*), or by an implied verb, as if he had said: "I mean, a tongue that is Arabic." He said: Some of them said it is governed by *musaddiq* (confirming), making the Book confirm the tongue.

According to the view of those who make *lisanan* an accusative of circumstance and consider it a description of the Book, the meaning should be: And this is a Book in an Arabic tongue, confirming the Torah, the Book of Musa, that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah, and that what he brought is from Allah and is true.

As for the second view that we related from some of them, that the word governing *lisanan* is *musaddiq*, it is a view without meaning, because if it is interpreted this way it would lead to the conclusion that what confirms the Qur'an is the Qur'an itself. There is no sense in saying: "And this is a Book that confirms itself," because the Arabic tongue is this very Book. Unless the "Arabic tongue" is taken to mean Muhammad (ﷺ), and the interpretation is directed to: "And this is a Book, which is the Qur'an, confirming Muhammad, who is the Arabic tongue." Then this would be one possible interpretation.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The phrase ﴿in the Arabic tongue﴾ is a description (*na't*) of the Book, and it is in the accusative because what is meant is: "And this is a Book confirming the Torah and the Gospel, in the Arabic tongue." So *lisanan 'arabiyyan* comes out from *musaddiq*, since that is a verb, as you say: "I passed by a man who stands well-doing" and "I passed by a standing man, well-doing." He said: If *lisanun 'arabiyyun* were in the nominative, it would be permissible as a description of the Book.

It has been mentioned that this is in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "And this is a Book confirming what is before it, in the Arabic tongue." According to this reading, the accusative in ﴿in the Arabic tongue﴾ can be explained in two ways: first, as I have shown, that the tongue is separate from the word ﴿confirming﴾; and second, that it is a detached accusative (*qat'*) from the pronoun in *bayna yadayhi* (before it).

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*hal*) of the mention of the Book within *musaddiq*, because the word ﴿confirming﴾ is a verb. So the interpretation of the speech, given that this is the case, is: "And this Qur'an confirms the Book of Musa, that Muhammad is a prophet sent, in the Arabic tongue."

\* \*

As for His words ﴿to warn those who have wronged﴾:

It means: this Book which We sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ) is to warn those who have wronged themselves by disbelieving in Allah and worshipping other than Him.

\* \*

As for His words ﴿and as good tidings for the doers of good﴾:

It means: it is good tidings for those who obeyed Allah and did good in their faith and in their obedience to Him in this world, so Allah will give them a good reward in the Hereafter for their obedience to Him. Regarding His words ﴿and good tidings﴾ (*wa bushra*), there are two grammatical possibilities (*wujhan min al-i'rab*): the nominative, as a conjunction with the Book, meaning: "And this is a Book confirming, and good tidings for the doers of good." And the accusative, with the meaning: "to warn those who have wronged, and to give good tidings." If one puts *yubashshira* (to give good tidings) or *bushra* or *bushara* in its place, it is put in the accusative, just as you say: "I came to you to visit you," and "a honour for you" (*karamatan laka*), "and a fulfilment of your right" (*qada'an li-haqqika*), meaning: "I came to visit you and honour you, and fulfil your right," so *karamah* and *qada'* are in the accusative by an implied verb.

The reciters differed in the reading of ﴿to warn﴾ (*liyundhira*). The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz read it *litundhira* with the letter *ta'* (you), meaning: "that you, O Muhammad, may warn." The majority of the reciters of Iraq read it with the letter *ya'* (he), meaning: "that the Book may warn." Whichever of the two readings a reciter uses, he is correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verses 13–14:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast — there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ (13) ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein forever, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ (14).

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾ — the One besides whom there is no god — ﴿and then remain steadfast﴾ — upon their affirmation of that, not mixing it with polytheism, and not disobeying Allah in His command and His prohibition — ﴿there will be no fear concerning them﴾ — from the terror of the Day of Resurrection and its horrors — ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ — over what they left behind after their death.

* *

And His saying ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying: those who said this statement and remained steadfast are the people of Paradise and its residents ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ — meaning: remaining therein eternally ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾ — meaning: a recompense from Us, which We gave them for their righteous deeds that they used to perform in the world.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 46, verse 15:

Concerning the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and weaning are thirty months. [He continues] until, when he reaches his maturity and reaches forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that You approve. And make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims."﴾ (15)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We enjoined upon the son of Adam good companionship with his parents during their lifetimes, and kindness to them both in their lifetimes and after their deaths.

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿ḥusnan﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it "ḥusnan" with a ḍammah on the ḥā', according to the interpretation described. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿iḥsānan﴾ with an alif, meaning: We enjoined him to act with kindness towards them both. Whichever of these a reciter reads is correct, since the meanings are close and each reading is widely transmitted among the reciters.

* *

His words ﴿His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We enjoined man to be good to his parents, kindness to them, because of what they did for him as a fetus, an infant and a young child. Then the Exalted described what he owed to his mother, and what she endured in his carrying and his birth, and alerted him to the duty of kindness owed to her, and her right to honor and fine companionship. So He said: ﴿His mother carried him﴾, meaning in her womb, ﴿with hardship﴾, meaning with difficulty, ﴿and gave birth to him with hardship﴾, meaning she bore him with difficulty.

As related:

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship﴾: she carried him in hardship and gave birth to him in hardship.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship﴾, they both said: she carried him in hardship and gave birth to him in hardship.

* Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿His mother carried him with hardship﴾, he said: hardship upon her.

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿karhan﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it "karhan" with a fatḥah on the kāf. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿kurhan﴾ with a ḍammah. I have already explained the disagreement among the reciters about the fatḥah and the ḍammah in Surah al-Baqarah, in a manner that makes repeating it here unnecessary.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are well-known readings with close meanings, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

* *

His words ﴿And his carrying and his weaning are thirty months﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: his mother's carrying him as a fetus in her womb, and her weaning him from nursing, and her ceasing to nurse him, together amount to thirty months.

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿wa-fiṣāluh﴾. The majority of the reciters of the major cities, apart from al-Hasan al-Basri, read ﴿wa-ḥamluhu wa-fiṣāluhu﴾, meaning: his mother separated him from nursing, a separation and weaning. It is reported that al-Hasan al-Basri used to read it "wa-ḥamluhu wa-faṣluhu" with a fatḥah on the fā' and no alif, meaning: his mother's weaning of him.

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is what the reciters of the major cities hold, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it, and the anomalousness of what contradicts it.

* *

His words ﴿until, when he reaches his maturity﴾

The people of interpretation differed about the duration of that limit in years. Some of them said: it is thirty-three years.

Those who said this:

* Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Idris told us, saying: I heard Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "His maturity" is thirty-three years, his full strength is forty years, and the span in which God established His proof against the son of Adam is sixty.

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿until, when he reaches his maturity﴾, he said: thirty-three.

Others said: it is reaching the age of puberty.

Those who said this:

* Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Mujalid informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "al-Ashudd" is the age of puberty, when good deeds are recorded for him and bad deeds are recorded against him.

We have previously explained that al-Ashudd is the plural of shidd, and that it refers to the culmination of his strength and his full maturity. Since this is so, thirty-three is closer to the meaning than puberty, because a person does not reach the full completion of his powers and the peak of his strength at the time of puberty. When the Arabs mention a pair of such things in speech and join one to the other, they make both times close to each other, as the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] almost two-thirds of the night, or half of it﴾. One would not normally say, "I know that you stand for a while close to an hour of the night and all of it," or "I took a little of the wealth or all of it," but rather, "I took most of my wealth or all of it." Likewise, in His words ﴿until, when he reaches his maturity and reaches forty years﴾, there is no doubt that linking forty to thirty-three is better and more fitting, since the intention is to bring the two close to each other in sequence, as opposed to linking [maturity] to fifteen or eighteen.

* *

His words ﴿and reaches forty years﴾

That is the time when God's proof upon him is complete, the ignorance of his youth departs from him, and he recognizes what God requires of him in the right of his parents' kindness.

As related:

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and reaches forty years﴾: and his evil deeds of the past have passed.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and reaches forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me"﴾ up to ﴿of the Muslims﴾: and his evil deeds of the past have passed.

* * *

His words ﴿He says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents"﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: this human being said, whom God has guided to his rightness and who recognized God's right upon him in what He obligated him regarding the kindness to his parents: ﴿My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor﴾, meaning: incite me to thank You for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me, in acquainting me with Your oneness, guiding me to acknowledge that, and to act in obedience to You, ﴿and upon my parents﴾ from before me, and other of Your favors upon us, and inspire me with that. The root of "awza'nī" is from "wazza'tu al-rajul 'alā kadhā," meaning: I impelled the man toward such-and-such.

Ibn Zayd used to say about this what has been related:

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿awza'nī an ashkura ni'matak﴾: "Make me thank Your favor." This is what Ibn Zayd said concerning ﴿rabbi awza'nī﴾, and although the meaning of the word leads to it, it is not the correct meaning of al-iwza'.

* * *

His words ﴿and that I do righteousness that You approve﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: enable me to do righteous deeds among the deeds that You approve, and that deed is by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger (ﷺ).

* * *

His words ﴿And make righteous for me my offspring﴾

He says: make my affairs righteous for me in my offspring whom You have granted me, by making them guides to faith in You, following Your good pleasure, and acting in obedience to You. Thus He described him, may He be exalted, as dutiful toward fathers and mothers, sons and daughters. It is related that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

* * *

His words ﴿Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, informing about the words of this human being: ﴿Indeed, I have repented to You﴾, meaning: I have repented to You from my sins that preceded from me in my past days. ﴿And indeed, I am of the Muslims﴾, meaning: and indeed I am among those who humble themselves to You in obedience, submitting to Your command and Your prohibition, and yielding to Your judgment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 16:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their evil deeds; they are among the companions of Paradise. [It is] the true promise which they were promised.﴾

His, may He be exalted, saying: Those whose description is this description are those from whom the best of their good deeds in the world is accepted, so He rewards them for it and recompenses them for it. ﴿And We overlook their evil deeds﴾ means: and He pardons them for the evil deeds they committed in the world, so He does not punish them for them. ﴿Among the companions of Paradise﴾ means: We do this with them, just as We did that with the companions of Paradise and its people, who are its people.

As:

* Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from al-Ghutrif, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), from the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibril), who said: "The good deeds and bad deeds of the servant are brought, and some of them are settled against others. If a good deed remains, Allah expands for him in Paradise." He said: I entered upon Yazdad, and he narrated a hadith like this. He said: I said: "And if the good deed is gone?" He said: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their evil deeds﴾ ... the verse.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: Abu Bakr called Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said to him: "I advise you with an advice, so memorise it: indeed Allah has a right at night which He does not accept in the day, and a right in the day which He does not accept at night. Indeed, there is no voluntary act for anyone until he fulfils the obligation. Indeed, the scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection are heavy only because of their following the truth in the world, and it was heavy for them; and it is right that a scale in which nothing but the truth is placed should be heavy. And the scales of those whose scales are light on the Day of Resurrection are light because of their following falsehood in the world, and it was light for them; and it is right that a scale in which nothing but falsehood is placed should be light."

Have you not seen that Allah mentioned the people of Paradise by their best deeds, so that one speaker might say: "How can my deed reach the deed of these people?" That is because Allah, mighty and majestic, overlooked their worst deeds and did not reveal them. Have you not seen that Allah mentioned the people of the Fire by their worst deeds, so that one speaker might say: "I am better in deed than these people?" That is because Allah rejected their best deeds for them. Have you not seen that Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down the verse of hardship alongside the verse of ease, and the verse of ease alongside the verse of hardship, so that the believer would be hopeful and fearful, lest he cast himself into destruction, and would not wish of Allah a wish in which he desires other than the truth from Him.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some reciters of Kufa recited ﴿yutaqabbalu wa yutajawwazu﴾ with the yā' of both vowelled with a ḍammah, in the passive form, with ﴿aḥsanu﴾ in the nominative. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited ﴿nataqabbalu wa natajāwazu﴾ with the nūn and its fatḥah, with ﴿aḥsana﴾ in the accusative, according to the meaning of Allah, may His praise be exalted, informing about Himself that He does this with them,

and as a return of the speech to His saying ﴿And We enjoined upon man﴾, [meaning] "and We accept from them the best of what they did and overlook." Both are well-known recitations, sound in meaning, and whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

* *

As for His saying ﴿the true promise which they were promised﴾:

It means: Allah made them this promise, a true promise, about which there is no doubt that He will fulfil it for them, which Allah, may He be exalted, promised them in the world. The phrase ﴿the true promise﴾ is in the accusative because it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) taken out of His saying ﴿We accept from them the best of what they did and overlook their evil deeds﴾. The verbal noun of "promised" was brought out of this speech as "promise," because His saying ﴿yataqabbalu ʿanhum wa yatajāwaz﴾ is a promise from Allah to them; so He said "the true promise," according to that meaning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 17:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿But he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both! Do you threaten me that I will be brought forth, when generations have passed before me?" While they both call upon Allah for help, [saying], "Woe to you! Believe, for indeed the promise of Allah is true." But he says, "This is not but the legends of the former peoples."﴾ (46:17)

This is a description from Allah, dhikruhu, of a man who is astray and a disbeliever, and undutiful toward his parents, while they both strive in advising him and calling him to Allah. Their call and their counsel only increase him in defiance and rebellion against Allah and in persistence in his ignorance. Allah, jalla thanauhu, says: ﴿But he who says to his parents﴾, meaning: in response to their call to faith in Allah and their affirmation of the resurrection of Allah's creation from their graves and His recompensing them for their deeds. ﴿Uff to you both﴾ means: filth and stench to you both. ﴿Do you threaten me that I will be brought forth﴾ means: do you threaten me that I will be brought out of my grave after my perishing and my decay in it, alive.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Do you threaten me that I will be brought forth﴾: that I will be resurrected after death.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Do you threaten me that I will be brought forth﴾, he said: it means the resurrection after death.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿But he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both! Do you threaten me"﴾ ... to the end of the verse; he said: The one who said this was a son of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. He said: ﴿Do you threaten me that I will be brought forth﴾: do you threaten me that I will be resurrected after death.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿But he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both! Do you threaten me that I will be brought forth"﴾, he said: He is the disbeliever, the wicked, undutiful to his parents, denying the resurrection.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Then He described a wicked servant, undutiful to his parents and wicked, so He said: ﴿But he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both!"﴾ ... to His words ﴿the legends of the former peoples﴾.

* * *

And His words ﴿while generations have passed before me﴾.

He means: "Do you threaten me that I will be resurrected, when generations of nations have passed before me and perished, and none of them has been resurrected? And if I were to be resurrected after my death as you both say, then those generations that perished before me would have been resurrected." ﴿While they both call upon Allah for help﴾: may He, dhikruhu, exalted is He, say that his parents were seeking Allah's help against him, and calling upon Him to aid them against him, that he would believe in Allah and affirm the resurrection, and they say to him: ﴿Woe to you! Believe﴾, meaning: affirm the promise of Allah and acknowledge that you will be resurrected after your death, for the promise of Allah, which He promised His creation, that He will raise them from their graves and bring them out of them to the place of reckoning to recompense them for their deeds, is true without any doubt. Then the enemy of Allah replies to his parents, rejecting their counsel and denying the promise of Allah, saying: "This that you both tell me and call me to, of belief that I will be resurrected from my grave after my death, is nothing but the falsehoods that the former people among mankind wrote down and recorded, and you both have found them and believed them."

"Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 18–19"

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those are they against whom the word has come into effect, among nations that passed away before them of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ (18) ﴿And for each are ranks according to what they did, and that He may fully repay them their deeds, and they will not be wronged.﴾ (19)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: These, whose description is this description, upon whom the punishment of God has become due, and upon whom His retribution and wrath have descended, are like those upon whom the punishment of God descended, in the same manner as what befell those nations of jinn and mankind who passed away before them, who denied the messengers of God and rebelled against the command of their Lord.

* *

And His saying ﴿Indeed, they were losers﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, they were the defrauded, by trading guidance for misguidance and bliss for punishment.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: "The jinn do not die." Qatadah said: I said, "﴿Those are they against whom the word has come into effect, among nations that passed away before them…﴾" ... the verse.

* *

And His saying ﴿And for each are ranks according to what they did﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: For each of these two groups, the group of faith in God and the Last Day and kindness to parents, and the group of disbelief in God and the Last Day and disobedience to parents, whose description our Lord, mighty and majestic, mentioned in these verses, there are stations and grades with God on the Day of Resurrection, according to what they did, meaning according to their deeds which they performed in the world, whether good, righteous or evil, for which God will recompense them.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And for each are ranks according to what they did﴾: "The ranks of the people of the Fire go downward, and the ranks of the people of Paradise go upward." ﴿And that He may fully repay them their deeds﴾ means: that He may give all of them the wages of their deeds which they did in the world, the good-doer among them according to his goodness, the honor God has promised, and the evil-doer among them according to his evil, the requital He has prepared. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ means: none of them will be wronged; the evil-doer among them is only punished for his sin, not for what he did not do, nor is the burden of another's sin placed upon him, and the good-doer among them is not deprived of the reward of his goodness.
