Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 20:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire: "You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them. So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation, because you were arrogant in the land without right, and because you used to defy (Allah)."﴾

His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire﴾ — it will be said to them: ﴿"You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them"﴾ in it.

As (narrated):

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire﴾, [Yazid] recited until reaching ﴿and because you used to defy (Allah)﴾. Qatadah said: "By Allah, there are people who stipulate their good deeds; a man reserves his good things, if he is able. There is no might nor power except by Allah."
It is mentioned that Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "If I wished, I could be the one among you with the finest food and the softest clothing, but I preserve my good things." It is also mentioned to us that when he arrived in Syria, a meal was prepared for him the like of which he had never seen before. He said: "This is for us; then what of the poor Muslims who died without ever being satisfied with barley bread?" Khalid ibn al-Walid said: "For them is Paradise." Umar's eyes filled with tears, and he said: "If our share is in worldly goods, and they have gone with Paradise, then they have separated from us by a far separation." Abu Ja'far said, as I see it: [this is the sense].

It is mentioned to us that "the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon the People of the Bench (Ahl al-Suffah), a place where the poor Muslims gathered, and they were patching their clothing with leather, having no patches for it. He said: 'You today are better, or the day when one of you goes out in one garment and comes back in another, and is brought a bowl of food in the morning and another in the evening, and his house is covered as the Ka'bah is covered.' They said: 'We are better on that day.' He said: 'Rather, you are better today.'"

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: A companion of ours related to us from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Our food with the Prophet (ﷺ) was only the two blacks: water and dates. By Allah, we did not see your wheat bread (samra') at all, and we did not know what it was."

* [Ibn Humayd?] said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Burdah ibn Abdullah ibn Qays al-Ash'ari, from his father, who said: "O my son, had you witnessed us with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and we were with our Prophet when rain struck us, you would have thought our smell was the smell of sheep; our clothing was only wool."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic, ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life﴾ ... to the end of the verse. Then he recited ﴿Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein﴾, and recited ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it﴾, and recited ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life), We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish﴾ ... to the end of the verse, and said: These are the ones who squandered their good things in their worldly life.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying ﴿You squandered﴾. The majority of the readers of the regional centres recited ﴿adhhabtum﴾ without interrogation, except Abu Ja'far al-Qari', who recited it with interrogation. The Arabs use interrogation for reproach and may omit the interrogative in such a context, saying: "adhhabta fa-fa'alta kadha wa kadha" and "dhahabta fa-fa'alta wa fa'alta." The recitation I prefer most is without interrogation, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it, and because it is the more eloquent of the two forms.

* *

As for His saying ﴿So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation﴾

His, may He be exalted, saying: It will be said to them: "So today, O disbelievers, who squandered your good things in your worldly life, you will be recompensed," that is, you will be requited with the punishment of humiliation, meaning the punishment of the Fire which will humiliate them.

As (narrated):

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the punishment of humiliation﴾, he said: "Humiliation." ﴿Because you were arrogant in the land without right﴾, meaning: because you were arrogant in the world upon the surface of the earth toward your Lord, refusing to make worship sincerely His, and to submit to His command and prohibition, without right, that is, without what your Lord permitted you and allowed you. ﴿And because you used to defy (Allah)﴾, meaning: because in it you used to oppose His obedience and so disobeyed Him.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And mention the brother of ʿAd, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf, and warners had passed away before him and after him, [saying], "Worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "And mention, O Muhammad, to your people who reject you what you have brought them of the truth: Hud, the brother of ʿAd. For Allah has sent you to them as He sent him to ʿAd. So warn them that there may befall them from Allah's vengeance for their disbelief what befell them when they denied Our messenger Hud sent to them, when he warned his people ʿAd in al-Ahqaf."

The Ahqaf (plural of ḥaqf, a term for sand that is elongated, not reaching the point of being a mountain) is what al-Aʿsha referred to:

فَباتَ إلى أرْطاةِ حِقْفٍ تَلُفُّهُ ... خَرِيقُ شَمالٍ يَتْرُكُ الوَجْهَ أقْتَما

[The verse is from al-Aʿsha of Banu Qays ibn Thaʿlaba (his Diwan, Cairo edition, p. 295), and in his narration "yalūdh" appears in place of "fabāt"; it is from a qasida praising Iyas ibn Qabisa al-Ta'i, or Qays ibn Maʿdi Karib, and the pronoun in "fabāt" refers to the wild bull to which he likened his she-camel, in earlier verses. Al-Artā: a large shrub growing in sand; its singular is artāa. What is bent and curved; its plural is aḥqāf, which is the point of evidence in the verse. Al-Kharīq: the violently blowing wind. Al-Shamāl: a cold wind blowing from the direction of Syria. He says: this bull takes refuge at an artāa in a bend of sand, around which a wild northern wind blows, leaving its face dusty and dark.]

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwil) differed about the place where these Ahqaf are. Some of them said: it is a mountain in Syria.

Mentioned by those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And mention the brother of ʿAd, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾, he said: al-Ahqaf: a mountain in Syria.

- I was told by al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying ﴿when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾: a mountain called al-Ahqaf.

Others said: rather, it is a valley between ʿUman and Mahra.

Mentioned by those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And mention the brother of ʿAd, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾, he said: al-Ahqaf, where Hud warned his people, is a valley between ʿUman and Mahra.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: The dwelling places of ʿAd and their community, where Allah sent Hud to them, were al-Ahqaf: the sand between ʿUman and Hadramawt, and all of Yemen. They had, in addition, spread throughout the whole earth, subduing its people by the excess of their strength which Allah had given them.

Others said: it is land.

Mentioned by those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, he said: al-Ahqaf: the land.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾, he said: Hashaf, or a word resembling it. Abu Musa said: they say mustahshif.

- al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾: Hishaf from Hismā.

Others said: they are sand dunes overlooking the sea at al-Shihr.

Mentioned by those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿And mention the brother of ʿAd, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾: it was mentioned to us that ʿAd were a tribe in Yemen, people of sand dunes overlooking the sea, in a land called al-Shihr.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿And mention the brother of ʿAd, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾, he said: We were told that they were in a land called al-Shihr, overlooking the sea, and they were people of sand.

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed us, from Saʿid ibn Abi Hilal, from ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Qatada, that he said: the dwellings of ʿAd were at al-Shihr.

The most correct of these sayings, in the view of truth, is to say: Allah, blessed and exalted, informed that ʿAd were warned by their brother Hud at al-Ahqaf, and al-Ahqaf is what has been described: elongated, raised sand dunes, as al-Ajjaj said:

بات إلى أرْطاةِ حقْف أحْقَفا

[I did not find this verse in the printed Diwan of al-Ajjaj. What appears in (Lisan al-ʿArab, ḥqf): "ihqawqafa al-raml": when it lengthened and curved. "Ihqawqafa al-hilal": it curved. Anything that lengthened and curved has ihqawqafa, like the back of a camel, or the figure of the moon; al-Ajjaj said: "A traveller whom fatigue has worn down, after what he endured ... the nights' passing, stage upon stage / until the crescent's halo curved." The author cited this verse as evidence that al-Ahqaf are elongated, raised sand dunes, as al-Ajjaj said: "bāt ... etc." It originates from the evidences of Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 222), where he said: "idh andhara qawmahu bi-l-Ahqaf": the sand dunes of the Ahqaf; al-Ajjaj said... the verse. I say: I am not certain of the soundness of this evidence, as most of its wording is from the preceding evidence, so it may have been garbled in the mouths of narrators and merged with the earlier one.]

And similarly:

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And mention the brother of ʿAd, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾: al-Ahqaf: sand that is like a mountain in shape, which the Arabs call a ḥaqf, and it is only called aḥqaf when it is sand. He said: The brother of ʿAd is Hud. It is possible that it was a mountain in Syria. It is possible that it was a valley between ʿUman and Hadramawt. It is possible that it was al-Shihr. Knowing its location is not an obligation, and ignorance of it is not a neglect of a duty; wherever it was, its description is what we have described: that they were a people whose dwellings were elevated, elongated sand.

* *

His saying: ﴿and warners had passed away before him and after him, [saying], "Worship none but Allah."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The messengers had passed away, warning their nations, ﴿before him﴾, meaning before Hud, ﴿and after him﴾, meaning after Hud. It has been mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud) it is: ﴿and warners had passed away before him and after him﴾. ﴿"Worship none but Allah"﴾ means: do not associate anything with Allah in your worship of Him, but devote worship sincerely to Him, and single Him out in divinity, for there is no god but Him. They were, as has been mentioned, people of idols which they worshipped besides Allah.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mentioned by those who said that:

- I was told by al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying ﴿and warners had passed away before him and after him, [saying], "Worship none but Allah"﴾: Allah sends no messenger except on the basis that Allah be worshipped.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, reports the words of Hud to his people: "Indeed, I fear for you, O people, because of your worship of other than Allah, the punishment of Allah on a tremendous day," and that is the Day of Resurrection, whose terror is great.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 46, verses 22–23:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? So bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful."﴾ (22)

Its meaning: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The people of ʿAd said to Hud, when he said to them, "Do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day": "O Hud, have you come to us to turn us away from the worship of our gods, toward the worship of that to which you call us, and to following you in your statement?"

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about that.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods?﴾, he said: "to remove us," and he recited ﴿He had almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in their worship﴾, he said: "to lead us astray, remove us, and turn us away." ﴿So bring us what you threaten us with﴾ of punishment for our worship of what we worship of gods. ﴿If you are﴾ among those truthful in his speech and his promises.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 46, verses 22–23:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? So bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful."﴾ (22)

Its meaning: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The people of ʿAd said to Hud, when he said to them, "Do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day": "O Hud, have you come to us to turn us away from the worship of our gods, toward the worship of that to which you call us, and to following you in your statement?"

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about that.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods?﴾, he said: "to remove us," and he recited ﴿He had almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in their worship﴾, he said: "to lead us astray, remove us, and turn us away." ﴿So bring us what you threaten us with﴾ of punishment for our worship of what we worship of gods. ﴿If you are﴾ among those truthful in his speech and his promises.

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "Knowledge of it is only with Allah, and I convey to you what I have been sent with. But I see you to be a people acting ignorantly."﴾ (23)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Hud said to his people, 'Ad: ﴿Knowledge is only with Allah﴾, meaning the knowledge of the time when the punishment from Allah that I promise you for your disbelief in Him will come. I know of that only what He has taught me. ﴿And I convey to you what I have been sent with﴾, meaning: I am only a messenger to you from Allah, a conveyer who delivers to you from Him what He has sent me with of the message. ﴿But I see you to be a people acting ignorantly﴾, meaning: you are ignorant of the places of your own benefit. You do not recognise the harm upon yourselves in worshipping other than Allah and in hastening His punishment.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Rather, it is that which you were impatient for: a wind within which is a painful punishment.﴾ (24)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When the punishment of Allah that they had hastened came to them, they saw it as a cloud spread across one side of the sky. ﴿Approaching their valleys﴾. The Arabs call a cloud that appears in one quarter of the sky in the evening, and by the next morning has spread out and drawn together into a single mass, an *'arid* (a cloud that stretches across the sky), because of its breadth across some part of the sky when it first forms, as al-A'sha said:

*O you who see a cloud, I spent the night watching it,*
*as though the lightning on its edges were flames.* [[The verse is by A'sha ibn Qays ibn Tha'labah (his Diwan, Cairo edition, p. 57). In his version, "ارقبه" is used in place of "ارمقه"; both mean "look at it". The verse is evidence that the meaning of *'arid* is a cloud crossing the sky. The lexicon *Lisan al-Arab* (root ع ر ض) says: "The *'arid* is a cloud that crosses the horizon of the sky. In the Revelation, concerning the people of 'Ad: 'When they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain",' meaning: they said, 'This is what we were promised, a cloud containing rain.'" End of quotation. Abu 'Ubaydah said in *Majaz al-Qur'an* (folio 222): "The *'arid* among clouds is that which is seen in one quarter of the sky in the evening, and by the morning it has spread out and become level."]]

﴿They said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."﴾ Because of what they saw, they supposed that rain had come to them by which they would be revived. So they said: this is what Hud had been promising us, and it is rain.

As reported:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys﴾ … to the end of the verse. It was mentioned to us that rain was withheld from them for a time, so when they saw the punishment coming towards them, ﴿they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."﴾ It was mentioned to us that they said, "Hud is a liar, Hud is a liar." When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) came out and they saw him, he said: ﴿Rather, it is that which you were impatient for: a wind within which is a painful punishment.﴾

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Allah drove the black cloud, which Qayl ibn 'Anz had chosen, with what it contained of vengeance, towards 'Ad, until it emerged upon them from a valley belonging to them called al-Mughith. When they saw it, they rejoiced, ﴿saying, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."﴾ Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Rather, it is that which you were impatient for: a wind within which is a painful punishment.﴾

* *

As for His words, ﴿Rather, it is that which you were impatient for﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, is reporting the words of His Prophet (ﷺ), Hud, to his people when they said to him, on seeing the cloud of punishment that had appeared to them in the sky, "This is a cloud bringing us rain by which we will be revived." He answered: it is not a cloud of rain, but a cloud of punishment for you. ﴿Rather, it is that which you were impatient for﴾, that is, it is the punishment you were impatient for when you said, ﴿"Bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful."﴾ ﴿A wind within which is a painful punishment﴾. The word "wind" is repeated, as in the phrase ﴿it is that which you were impatient for﴾, as though it were said: "Rather, it is a wind within which is a painful punishment."

The people of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: Hud was strong among his people, and he was sitting among his people when a dark, lowering cloud came. ﴿They said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." He said, "Rather, it is that which you were impatient for: a wind within which is a painful punishment."﴾ He said: Then a wind came and began to hurl down the tents, and it would lift up a man who was absent and throw him down.

• Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Sulayman said: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: The wind would carry the litter-rider and lift her up until she looked like a locust.

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys﴾ … to the end of the verse. He said: It is the wind when it stirs up a cloud. ﴿They said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."﴾ Then their prophet said: "Rather, it is a wind within which is a painful punishment."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 25:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It will destroy everything by the command of its Lord, and by morning there was nothing to be seen but their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.﴾

As for His saying ﴿It will destroy everything by the command of its Lord﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: it will ruin everything, and cast some of it upon other parts, so that it destroys it, as Jarir said:

"And it was for you like the camel of Thamud when ... it roared, its back, and so it destroyed them with destruction."

[[The line is not by Jarir as it appears in the original; it belongs to al-Farazdaq, from a qasida in his Diwan in which he answers Jarir and contradicts him. It is in his Diwan (Sawi edition, p. 442), and the opening of the qasida is: "He dragged the disgraceful deeds upon Kulayb ... Jarir, then what prevented him from defending [his people]?"

"And it was for them like the camel of Thamud when ... it roared, its back, and so it destroyed them with destruction."

That is, it brought ruin and devastation upon his people.]]

By His saying "destroyed them" he means: cast some of them upon others, slain and perished.

And what is meant by His saying ﴿It will destroy everything by the command of its Lord﴾ is everything it was sent to destroy, for it did not destroy Hud and those who believed in him.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Talq narrated to us, from Za'idah, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah did not send upon 'Ad any wind except as much as the size of this ring of mine, and he took off his ring.

* *

As for His saying ﴿by morning there was nothing to be seen but their dwellings﴾:

He says: the people of Hud awoke, having been destroyed and perished, so that nothing was seen in their lands except their dwellings in which they used to live.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying ﴿by morning there was nothing to be seen but their dwellings﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited ﴿لا تَرَى إلا مَساكِنَهُمْ﴾ with the ta' and the accusative (nasb), meaning: "by morning you, O Muhammad, saw nothing but their dwellings." The majority of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿لا يُرَى إِلا مَسَاكِنُهُمْ﴾ with the ya' in "yura" and the nominative for "masakinuhum," meaning: what I described before, that nothing was seen in their lands except their dwellings.

It was also narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri as "lā turā" with the ta'. Whichever of the two recitations of the people of Medina and Kufa the reader adopts, he is correct: the nominative for the dwellings when it is recited "yura" with the ya' and damma, and the accusative for the dwellings when it is recited "tara" with the ta' and fatha. As for the reading attributed to al-Hasan, it is ugly in Arabic, though permissible. It is ugly because the Arabs make the verb before "illa" masculine even when the nouns after it are feminine. They say: "ma qama illa ukhtuka" (none stood but your sister), "ma ja'ani illa jariyatuka" (none came to me but your slave-girl), and they hardly ever say "ma ja'atni illa jariyatuka." This is because what is omitted before "illa" is either "ahad" (someone) or "shay'" (something), and the Arabs make the verb that goes with these masculine even when they refer to a feminine, so they say: "in ja'aka minhunna ahad fa-akrimhu" (if any one of them comes to you, honour him), and they do not say "in ja'atka." Al-Farra' permitted it as a reluctant usage, and mentions that al-Mufaddal recited to him:

"And our fire, no fire has been seen like it, Ma'add knows this, the most honourable."

[[This line is among the evidences of al-Farra' in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 301), cited at the words "fa-asbahu la turā illā masākinahum," where he said it was recited with the ta' or with the ya' vocalized (with the verb in the passive). He described the recitation with the vocalized ta' as having ugliness; he said: "Because when the Arabs place the feminine verb before 'illa' they make it masculine, so they say: 'lam yaqum illa jariyatuka' and 'ma qama illa jariyatuka,' and they hardly ever say 'ma qamat illa jariyatuka,' because what is left out (the excepted-from) is 'ahad' or 'shay',' and 'ahad,' if it is for a feminine or masculine, its verb is masculine. Do you not see that you say: 'in qama ahadun minhunna fa-idribhu,' and you do not say: 'in qamat illa mustakrahan'? It is permissible in that way. He said: al-Mufaddal recited to me: 'And our fire ...' the line. So the verb is feminine because it refers to the fire; and the best speech is to say: 'ma ru'iya mithluha.'" I say: his words "akramā" are an adjective of "nāranā."]]

So he made the verb feminine, because it refers to the fire, and he said: the best speech is to say: "ma ru'iya mithluha."

* *

As for His saying ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: just as We requited 'Ad, for their disbelief in Allah, with punishment in this worldly life, and We destroyed them with Our chastisement, so likewise We recompense the people among Our creatures who disbelieve in Allah, when they persist in their error and rebel against their Lord.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 26:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you, and We made for them hearing and sight and hearts, but their hearing and their sight and their hearts did not avail them anything, since they were rejecting the signs of Allah, and there encompassed them that which they used to ridicule.﴾

He, may He be remembered, says to the disbelievers of Quraysh: "And We had established, O people, [the people of] ʿAd, whom We destroyed for their disbelief, in that wherein We have not established you of the world, and We gave them of it what We did not give you: abundance of wealth, expansiveness of bodies, and strength of bodies."

Those of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) said the same as what we have said concerning that.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to me, he said: Muawiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you﴾: he says, "We did not establish you."

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you﴾: "He informed you that He gave the people what He did not give you."

* *

And His words ﴿And We made for them hearing﴾

[They would] hear with it the admonitions of their Lord, and sight with which they would see the proofs of Allah, and hearts with which they would understand what would delight and benefit them. ﴿But their hearing and their sight and their hearts did not avail them anything﴾: he says, their hearing, sight and hearts that He had given them did not benefit them, since they did not use them for what they were given for, and did not act with them in what would save them from the punishment of Allah, but rather they used them for what brought them closer to His wrath. ﴿Since they were rejecting the signs of Allah﴾: he says, since they were denying the proofs of Allah, namely His messengers, and denying their prophethood. ﴿And there encompassed them that which they used to ridicule﴾: he says, what they mocked returned upon them, and what they scorned descended upon them, since they had sought to hasten it as punishment. This is a warning from Allah, exalted is His praise, to Quraysh, saying to them: "Beware lest there befall you punishment like that which befell ʿAd, on account of your disbelief in Allah and your denial of His messengers, and hasten to repentance before vengeance."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verses 27–28:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We have destroyed the towns around you, and We have varied the signs that they might return.﴾ (27) ﴿Why then did those whom they had taken as gods besides Allah, as a means of approach, not help them? Rather, they strayed from them. That was their falsehood and what they used to fabricate.﴾ (28)

He, the Exalted, says to the disbelievers of Quraysh, warning them of His punishment and might, that it may descend upon them in their disbelief: ﴿And We have destroyed﴾ O people, the towns around your town, such as the place of the Thamud's rock, the land of Sodom, Ma'rib and the like. We warned their people with the exemplary punishments, and We ruined their dwellings, so that they lay fallen upon their roofs.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We have varied the signs﴾

It means: We admonished them with various kinds of admonition, and reminded them with many forms of remembrance and proofs, and We made that clear to them.

As related:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And We have varied the signs﴾: "He explained them." ﴿That they might return﴾: meaning, that they might turn back from what they were persisting in of disbelief in Allah and His signs.

In the speech there is an omitted part, left out because the context points to it, and it is: they refused except to persist in their disbelief and to continue in their error, so We destroyed them, and no helper from Us will help them. He, may His praise be exalted, says: Then why did the idols and gods of those former nations whom We destroyed not help them, those which they had taken to worship as a means of approach, by which they claimed to draw near to their Lord from Us when Our punishment came upon them, so that they might rescue them from Our torment, if they were to intercede for them with their Lord as they claimed.

This is an argument from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ against the polytheists of his people. He says to them: If your gods whom you worship besides Allah could avail you anything, or benefit you with Allah, as you claim you worship them only to bring you near to Allah in nearness, they would have availed those before you among the nations whom I destroyed for worshipping them, and would have repelled the punishment from them when it descended, or would have interceded for them with their Lord. Yet they were upon the same worship as you are upon, but those gods harmed them and did not benefit them.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Rather, they strayed from them﴾: meaning, their gods that they used to worship abandoned them, and went off in a direction other than theirs, because their worshippers were destroyed, while the gods were stones or copper, so what befell them did not touch the gods; they called upon them, but they did not answer them nor relieve them. That is their straying from them. ﴿That was their falsehood﴾: meaning, that was their lie which they used to tell, saying "these are our gods," ﴿and what they used to fabricate﴾: meaning, that is what they used to invent, saying "they bring us near to Allah in nearness, and they are our intercessors with Allah." The speech is expressed in the form of the verbal action while the intended meaning is the object, so it is said: "That was their falsehood," and the intended meaning is what was falsely attributed, because falsehood is really the act of the one who fabricates, while the gods are that by which falsehood was attributed. The explanation of similar cases has already passed before. He said: And likewise His saying ﴿and what they used to fabricate﴾.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying ﴿That was their falsehood﴾. The majority of the readers of the regional centers recited it as "wa-dhalika ifkuhum," with a kasra on the alif, a sukun on the fa', and a damma on the kaf, with the meaning we have explained.

It is related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, concerning this:

⁕ Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Awf, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn Abbas, that he used to recite it "wa-dhalika afkuhum," meaning with a fatha on the alif and the kaf, and he said: "It misled them."

Whoever recites the reading upon which the readers of the regional centers agree, the ha' and mim are in the genitive position. Whoever recites this reading that we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas, the ha' and mim are in the accusative position, because the meaning of the speech according to it is: "and that turned them away from belief in Allah."

The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is the reading upon which the readers of the regional centers agree, due to the consensus of the authorities upon it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verses 27–28:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We have destroyed the towns around you, and We have varied the signs that they might return.﴾ (27) ﴿Why then did those whom they had taken as gods besides Allah, as a means of approach, not help them? Rather, they strayed from them. That was their falsehood and what they used to fabricate.﴾ (28)

He, the Exalted, says to the disbelievers of Quraysh, warning them of His punishment and might, that it may descend upon them in their disbelief: ﴿And We have destroyed﴾ O people, the towns around your town, such as the place of the Thamud's rock, the land of Sodom, Ma'rib and the like. We warned their people with the exemplary punishments, and We ruined their dwellings, so that they lay fallen upon their roofs.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We have varied the signs﴾

It means: We admonished them with various kinds of admonition, and reminded them with many forms of remembrance and proofs, and We made that clear to them.

As related:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And We have varied the signs﴾: "He explained them." ﴿That they might return﴾: meaning, that they might turn back from what they were persisting in of disbelief in Allah and His signs.

In the speech there is an omitted part, left out because the context points to it, and it is: they refused except to persist in their disbelief and to continue in their error, so We destroyed them, and no helper from Us will help them. He, may His praise be exalted, says: Then why did the idols and gods of those former nations whom We destroyed not help them, those which they had taken to worship as a means of approach, by which they claimed to draw near to their Lord from Us when Our punishment came upon them, so that they might rescue them from Our torment, if they were to intercede for them with their Lord as they claimed.

This is an argument from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ against the polytheists of his people. He says to them: If your gods whom you worship besides Allah could avail you anything, or benefit you with Allah, as you claim you worship them only to bring you near to Allah in nearness, they would have availed those before you among the nations whom I destroyed for worshipping them, and would have repelled the punishment from them when it descended, or would have interceded for them with their Lord. Yet they were upon the same worship as you are upon, but those gods harmed them and did not benefit them.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Rather, they strayed from them﴾: meaning, their gods that they used to worship abandoned them, and went off in a direction other than theirs, because their worshippers were destroyed, while the gods were stones or copper, so what befell them did not touch the gods; they called upon them, but they did not answer them nor relieve them. That is their straying from them. ﴿That was their falsehood﴾: meaning, that was their lie which they used to tell, saying "these are our gods," ﴿and what they used to fabricate﴾: meaning, that is what they used to invent, saying "they bring us near to Allah in nearness, and they are our intercessors with Allah." The speech is expressed in the form of the verbal action while the intended meaning is the object, so it is said: "That was their falsehood," and the intended meaning is what was falsely attributed, because falsehood is really the act of the one who fabricates, while the gods are that by which falsehood was attributed. The explanation of similar cases has already passed before. He said: And likewise His saying ﴿and what they used to fabricate﴾.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying ﴿That was their falsehood﴾. The majority of the readers of the regional centers recited it as "wa-dhalika ifkuhum," with a kasra on the alif, a sukun on the fa', and a damma on the kaf, with the meaning we have explained.

It is related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, concerning this:

⁕ Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Awf, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn Abbas, that he used to recite it "wa-dhalika afkuhum," meaning with a fatha on the alif and the kaf, and he said: "It misled them."

Whoever recites the reading upon which the readers of the regional centers agree, the ha' and mim are in the genitive position. Whoever recites this reading that we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas, the ha' and mim are in the accusative position, because the meaning of the speech according to it is: "and that turned them away from belief in Allah."

The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is the reading upon which the readers of the regional centers agree, due to the consensus of the authorities upon it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 29:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when We turned toward you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an. So when they attended it, they said, "Listen attentively." And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners.﴾

Exalted is He, reprimanding the disbelievers of Quraysh for their disbelief in what the jinn believed, says: ﴿And when We turned toward you﴾ O Muhammad ﴿a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an﴾. It is mentioned that they were turned toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) because of the event that occurred, namely their being pelted with shooting stars.

Those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ziyad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The jinn used to listen, but when they were pelted they said: 'Surely this which has happened in the sky is something that has happened on earth.' So they went seeking until they saw the Prophet (ﷺ) coming out of the market of Ukaz, leading his companions in the dawn prayer, and they went back to their people."

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, the sky was guarded, and the Devil said: 'It is only guarded for a matter that has happened on earth.' So he sent his detachments throughout the earth, and they found the Prophet (ﷺ) standing, praying the dawn prayer with his companions at Nakhla, and he was reciting. They listened until he finished, [then] ﴿they went back to their people as warners﴾ ... to His words ﴿straight﴾."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And when We turned toward you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an﴾ ... to the end of the verse, he said: The sky was not guarded during the interval between 'Isa and Muhammad (ﷺ), and they used to sit in places for listening. But when Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ), the sky was guarded with a severe guard, and the devils were pelted, so they disapproved of that and said: ﴿We do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾. Then Iblis said: "Something has happened on earth," and the jinn gathered to him. He said: "Disperse throughout the earth and inform me of this news that has happened in the sky." The first group sent was a caravan from the people of Nasibin, who were the nobles and chiefs of the jinn, and he sent them to Tihama. They pressed on until they reached the valley, the Valley of Nakhla, and they found the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) praying the morning prayer in the bottom of Nakhla, so they listened; and when they heard him reciting the Qur'an, they said: "Listen attentively." The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) did not know that they had listened to him while he was reciting the Qur'an. When he concluded, they went back to their people as warners.

The scholars of interpretation differed concerning the number of the company whom Allah mentioned in His words ﴿We turned toward you a company of the jinn﴾. Some of them said: they were seven.

Those who said this:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And when We turned toward you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an﴾ ... the verse, he said: They were seven men from the people of Nasibin, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made them messengers to their people.

Others said: rather, they were nine men.

Those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, regarding ﴿And when We turned toward you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an﴾, he said: They were nine men, among them Zawba'a.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: "It was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in the bottom of Nakhla, ﴿So when they attended it﴾," he said: "They were nine, one of them Zawba'a."

* *

As for His words ﴿So when they attended it﴾:

That is: when this company of the jinn whom Allah turned toward His Messenger, the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), attended.

The scholars differed concerning the manner of their attending the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some of them said: they attended the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seeking to learn the matter that had happened before them in the sky, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not aware of their location, as we have already mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas.

And as for what has been narrated:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And when We turned toward you a company of the jinn﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not aware of them until they came, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed to him concerning them and informed him about them.

Others said: rather, the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to recite the Qur'an to them, and they were gathered for him after Allah had commanded him to warn them and ordered him to recite the Qur'an to them.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And when We turned toward you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an﴾, he said: "It has been mentioned to us that they were turned toward him from Nineveh. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I have been commanded to recite the Qur'an to the jinn, so which of you will follow me?' They lowered their heads. He asked them again a second time, and they lowered their heads. He asked them a third time, and they lowered their heads. A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you are indeed eager [[In Ibn Kathir it is "dhu nadbah" (ardent), and the man seems to be amazed at the Messenger's alacrity and haste when he summoned his companions to it, and they held back. It may be derived from their saying "rajul nadab," meaning a man quick and swift in need.]]' So Abdullah ibn Mas'ud followed him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered a mountain pass called the Pass of al-Hajun. He said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) drew a line around Abdullah to keep him within it. He said: I saw things like vultures walking in their wings, and I heard a loud clamor until I feared for the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ). Then he recited the Qur'an. When the Prophet of Allah returned, I said: 'O Prophet of Allah, what was the clamor I heard?' He said: 'They gathered before me over a slain man who was among them, and judgment was passed between them with truth.'

It has been mentioned to us that when Ibn Mas'ud came to Kufa, he saw elderly men with gray hair from the Zutt, and he was alarmed. He said: 'Who are these?' They said: 'These are a group of non-Arabs.' He said: 'I have not seen among those to whom the Prophet (ﷺ) conveyed Islam from the jinn anything more similar than these.'

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) went with Ibn Mas'ud one night when he invited the jinn. The Prophet (ﷺ) drew a line for Ibn Mas'ud and said to him: "Do not leave it." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) went to the jinn, recited the Qur'an to them, and then returned to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "Did you see anything?" He said: "I heard a loud clamor." He said: "The jinn quarreled over a slain man who was killed among them, and judgment was passed between them with truth." They asked him for provisions, and he said: "Every bone for you has flesh, and every dung for you is fodder." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, people find them disgusting for us." So the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade cleaning oneself with either of them. When Ibn Mas'ud came to Kufa and saw the Zutt, who are tall black people, he was alarmed, and said: "Have they appeared?" It was said to him: "These are a people of the Zutt." He said: "How much they resemble the company who were turned toward the Prophet (ﷺ)."

He said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Ghaylan al-Thaqafi, that he said to Ibn Mas'ud: "I have heard that you were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the delegation of the jinn." He said: "Indeed." He said: "How was it?" So he related the whole narration. It is mentioned that the Prophet (ﷺ) drew a line around him and said: "Do not leave it." It is mentioned that a black cloud like a dust storm covered the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he was terrified three times. When it was near dawn, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me and said: "Did you sleep?" I said: "No, by Allah, and I had intended many times to call for help from the people until I heard you striking them with your staff, saying: 'Sit down.'" He said: "Had you come out, I would not have been safe from some of them snatching you away." Then he said: "Did you see anything?" He said: "Yes, I saw black men wearing white garments." He said: "Those were the jinn of Nasibin. They asked me for provisions, and provisions means food. I supplied them with every dry bone, dung, or dropping." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what good is that to them?" He said: "Indeed, they will not find a bone but they will find meat on it as on the day it was eaten, nor a dropping but they will find grain in it as on the day it was eaten. So none of you should cleanse himself with a bone, dung, or dropping when he comes out from the privy."

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Abu Zur'ah Wahb ibn Rashid informed us, saying: Yunus said, Ibn Shihab said: Abu 'Uthman ibn Shubbah al-Khuza'i informed me, and he was from the people of Syria, that Ibn Mas'ud said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions while he was in Mecca: "Whoever among you wishes to attend the affair of the jinn tonight, let him do so." None of them attended except me. He said: We set out until, when we were at the upper part of Mecca, he drew a line for me with his foot and then commanded me to sit within it. Then he went on until he stood and began the recitation of the Qur'an. Large dark shapes overtook him, blocking me from him until I could not hear his voice. Then they began to disperse like pieces of cloud, going away, until only a group remained. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished at dawn, then went off to relieve himself, and then came to me and said: "What did the group do?" I said: "They are those people, O Messenger of Allah." He took a bone, or dung, or a skull, and gave it to them as provisions, then forbade anyone to clean himself with a bone or dung.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu 'Uthman ibn Shubbah al-Khuza'i, who was from the people of Syria, that 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned the same thing, except that he said: "He gave them dung or a bone as provisions," and he did not mention the skull.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: Yunus informed me, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, that Ibn Mas'ud said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "I spent the night reciting the Qur'an to the jinn, a quarter of it, at al-Hajun."

They differed concerning the place where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the Qur'an to them. 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said that he recited to them at al-Hajun, and we have already mentioned the report from him to that effect.

Others said: he recited to them at Nakhla, and we have already mentioned some who said that, and we will mention those we have not mentioned.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Khallad narrated to us, from Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the company who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the jinn of Nasibin came to him while he was at Nakhla.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And when We turned toward you a company of the jinn﴾, he said: He met them at Nakhla that night.

* *

As for His words ﴿So when they attended it, they said, "Listen attentively."﴾

He, exalted is He, says: when they attended the Qur'an while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reciting, some of them said to others: "Listen attentively, so that we may hear the Qur'an."

As:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, regarding ﴿So when they attended it, they said, "Listen attentively."﴾ They said: "Sah" (be quiet).

He said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So when they attended it, they said, "Listen attentively."﴾ He said: The people knew that they would not understand unless they were silent.

* *

As for His words ﴿So when it was concluded﴾:

That is: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the recitation and the reading of the Qur'an.

The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿So when it was concluded﴾, he said: when he finished the prayer. ﴿They went back to their people as warners.﴾

* *

As for His words ﴿They went back to their people as warners﴾:

That is: they returned warning them of Allah's punishment for disbelieving in Him.

It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made them messengers to their people.

Abu Kurayb narrated this to us, and they said: 'Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas. This statement contradicts the statement reported from him, that he said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) did not know that they had listened to him while he was reciting the Qur'an, because it is impossible that he would send them to others unless he had first known their location. Unless it is said that he did not know their location while they were listening to the Qur'an, then he knew afterward, before they returned to their people, and so he sent them as messengers to their people at that time; but that is not what the report narrated says.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 30:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it; it guides to the truth and to a straight path."﴾

His exalted words mean: reporting the statement of those jinn who were turned toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to their people, when they returned to them from the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ﴿O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses⁠—a Book⁠—confirming what was before it﴾. He says: it confirms what came before it of the Books of Allah which He sent down upon His messengers. [[In the original: "rasulihi" (His messenger); it is likely a copyist's error.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿it guides to the truth﴾:

He says: it guides to what is right, and indicates what is pleasing to Allah. ﴿And to a straight path﴾: He says: and to a path with no crookedness in it, which is Islam.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that he recited ﴿They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it; it guides to the truth and to a straight path."﴾ Then he said: How quickly these people understood! It has been reported to us that they were turned toward him from Nineveh.

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of God's, the Exalted's, words:

﴿O our people, respond to the caller of God and believe in him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment. And whoever does not respond to the caller of God, he cannot escape on earth, and he has no protectors apart from Him. Those are in clear error.﴾

God, exalted is His remembrance, reports about the words of this group of jinn: ﴿O our people, from among the jinn, respond to the caller of God﴾. They said: respond to the Messenger of God, Muhammad, in what he calls you to, of obedience to God. ﴿And believe in him﴾: that is, confirm him in what he has brought you from God's command and prohibition, and other things to which he has called you to affirm. ﴿He will forgive you﴾: that is, your Lord will cover over your sins for you, concealing them and not disgracing you with them in the Hereafter by punishing you for them. ﴿And protect you from a painful punishment﴾: that is, He will rescue you from a painful torment if you repent of your sins and turn from your disbelief to faith in God and in His caller.

* *

And His saying ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of God, he cannot escape on earth﴾

God, exalted is His remembrance, reports about the words of this group to their people: And whoever, O people, does not respond to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), Muhammad, and to his caller to what he was sent to call to, of monotheism and acting in obedience to Him. ﴿He cannot escape on earth﴾: that is, he cannot escape his Lord by fleeing, if He wishes to punish him for denying His caller and failing to confirm him, even if he goes off fleeing on the earth, for wherever he is, he is under His authority and power. ﴿And he has no protectors apart from Him﴾: that is, for whoever does not respond to the caller of God, there are no helpers apart from his Lord who can defend him against God if his Lord punishes him for his disbelief in Him and his denial of His caller.

* *

And His saying ﴿Those are in clear error﴾

That is: those who did not respond to the caller of God by confirming Him, and what He called them to of God's monotheism and acting in obedience to Him, are in deviation from the right path, taking a crooked way that is not upright. ﴿Clear﴾: that is, it becomes evident to whoever reflects on it that it is error and a way that does not aim at the right course.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 33:

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is Able to do all things.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Do these deniers not look at Allah's bringing back to life of His creatures after their death, and His raising them from their graves after their decay, those who said to their fathers and mothers: ﴿Uff to you both! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth, when generations have passed before me?﴾ Thus they were not raised with the sight of their hearts, so that they might see and know that Allah, who created the seven heavens and the earth, originated them from nothing, and was not wearied by bringing them into being, and so is not incapable of inventing and producing them. ﴿Is not able to give life to the dead﴾, so that He brings them forth, after their decay in their graves, alive as they were before their death.

The scholars of Arabic grammar differed regarding the reason for the entry of the particle bā' (ب) in His saying ﴿bi-qādirin﴾ (able). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: this bā' is like the bā' in His saying ﴿Sufficient is Allah﴾ (kafā bi-llāh), and it is like ﴿grows with the oil﴾ (tanbutu bi-l-duhn). Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: this bā' entered for negation (al-jaḥd). He said: the Arabs introduce it with negation when it raises what precedes it, and they introduce it when a verb is followed by something requiring two nouns, such as your saying: mā aẓunnuka bi-qā'imin (I do not think you are standing), mā aẓunnu annaka bi-qā'imin, and mā kunta bi-qā'imin (you were not standing). So when you remove the bā', you put in the accusative the element that it governed, by the verb that governs it. He said: if the bā' were dropped from qādir in this position, it would be nominative, because it is the predicate of inna. He said: one of them recited to me:

﴿fa-mā raja'at bi-khā'ibatin rikābun ... ḥakīmu bnu l-Musayyabi muntahāhā﴾ [[This line is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 303). He said: His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Do they not see that Allah who created the heavens and the earth is qādir?﴾: the bā' entered for the lām (of emphasis). The Arabs introduce it with negation when it raises what precedes it, or they introduce it when a verb is followed by something requiring two nouns, such as your saying: mā aẓunnuka bi-qā'imin, mā aẓunnu bi-qā'imin, and mā kunta bi-qā'imin. When the bā' is removed, you put in the accusative the element it governed, by the verb governing it. If the bā' were dropped from qādir in this position, it would be nominative, because it is the predicate of inna. One of them recited to me: "fa-mā raja'at bi-khā'ibatin... (the line)". So the bā' enters a verb which, if removed, would be governed by the verb and not by the bā'. This is analogous to what resembles it.]]

So the bā' enters a verb which, if it were removed, would be governed in the accusative by the verb and not by the bā'; what resembles this is treated by analogy.

Some who rejected the view of the Basran grammarian we have mentioned said: this bā' entered for negation, because the negated element in meaning, although separated between them by "inna" (that), is ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead?﴾ He said: the subject of "yaraw" (they see) and what follows it is in its complement, and the bā' does not enter upon it, but its meaning is negation, so the bā' entered for the meaning.

It is related from the Basran that he refused the entry of illā (except) after an oath's response, whereas the grammarians of Kufa permit it, saying: mā ẓanantu anna Zaydan illā qā'iman (I did not think Zayd was anything but standing), and mā ẓanantu anna Zaydan bi-'ālimin. And they recite:

﴿wa-lastu bi-ḥālifin law waladtu minhum ... ʿalā ʿammiyyatin illā Ziyādan﴾ [[This line was not attributed by the author, who transmitted it from some grammarians. It is not in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an. It is a point of disagreement between the Basrans and the Kufans: the Basrans refuse the entry of illā after the response to an oath, while the Kufans permit it and cite the line as evidence, as the author said.]]

He said: illā entered after the response to the oath. As for "kafā bi-llāh", this was introduced only for a sound meaning, which is exclamation (al-ta'ajjub), as you say: laẓurufa bi-Zaydin (how eloquent is Zayd!). He said: as for ﴿tanbutu bi-l-duhn﴾, they agreed that it is an extraneous (ṣila) particle. The most likely of the views regarding the correct position is the view of the one who said: the bā' in His saying ﴿bi-qādirin﴾ entered for negation, for the reasons we have mentioned to its proponents.

The reciters differed in reading His saying ﴿bi-qādirin﴾. The majority of the reciters of the cities, from Abu Ishaq, al-Jahdari and al-A'raj, recited ﴿bi-qādirin﴾, and this is the correct reading in our view, due to the consensus of the reciters of the cities upon it. As for the others I mentioned, it is reported that they used to recite it as "yaqdir" with a yā'. It is also mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud it is ﴿that Allah who created the heavens and the earth is qādir﴾ without the bā', and in that there is evidence for the one who recites "bi-qādirin" with the bā' and the alif.

* *

And His saying ﴿Yes, indeed He is Able to do all things﴾.

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Yes, He who created the heavens and the earth is able to give life to the dead; that is, He who created that over every thing He wills to create and intends to do, is possessed of power, nothing He intends prevents Him, and nothing He intends to do wearies Him, so the bringing of creation into being after annihilation does not weary Him, for whoever is incapable of that is weak, and it is not fitting that one who is weak in what he intends should be a god.

It is said concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire, [it will be said]: "Is this not the truth?" They will say: "Yes, by our Lord!" He will say: "So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾

Says He, exalted is His remembrance: And on the Day when these deniers of the Resurrection, and of God's reward for His servants for their righteous deeds and His punishment of them for their evil deeds, are exposed to the Fire, the Fire of Jahannam, it will be said to them at that time: "Is not this the punishment which you are being punished with today, and which you used to deny in the world, the truth?" This is a rebuke from God to them for their denial of it while they were in the world. ﴿They will say: "Yes, by our Lord!"﴾ Meaning: these disbelievers will answer immediately, saying, "Yes, it is the truth, by God." ﴿He will say: "So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾ Meaning: the One who makes them acknowledge this will say to them: "Taste now the punishment of the Fire for what you used to deny in the world, and reject, and refuse to acknowledge when you were called to believe in it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 46, verse 35:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient, and do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them. On the Day they see what they are promised, [it will be as if] they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day. [This is] a notification, so will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾

Exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), affirming him in persisting with what He has entrusted him with of the burden of the message and the weight of the loads of prophethood (ﷺ), and commanding him to take as an example, in resolving to carry on with that, the steadfast messengers (ulu al-azm) before him, who were patient over the great hardships they encountered from their peoples, and the harms and calamities they suffered from them. ﴿So be patient﴾, O Muhammad, over what has befallen you for the sake of God of harm from your deniers among your people, to whom We sent you with warning. ﴿As the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾ in carrying out God's command and submitting to His obedience, from among His messengers who did not let the severity they encountered prevent them from carrying out His command. It was said: the steadfast ones among them were those who were tested in the matter of God in this world with trials, and the trials did not increase them except in earnestness regarding God's command, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and those like them.

It was in a similar manner to what we have said that the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) spoke.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Thawabah ibn Mas'ud narrated to me, from Ata al-Khurasani, that he said regarding ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and Muhammad (ﷺ).

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾: "We used to narrate that Abraham was among them."

Ibn Zayd used to say the following about it:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾: "All the messengers were steadfast; God did not take a messenger except that he was one of resolve, so be patient as they were patient."

* Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Raja' narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾: He said: "God named it resolve from its severity."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them﴾:

It means: do not seek to hasten the punishment upon them; that is, do not hurry in asking your Lord for that for them, for it will certainly descend upon them. ﴿On the Day they see what they are promised, [it will be as if] they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day﴾: meaning, on the day they see God's punishment which He promised them He would bring down upon them, they will have stayed in the world only an hour of a day, because it will make them forget the severity of the punishment that descends upon them, in comparison with how long they remained in the world and the sum of the years and months they dwelt there, as He, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿He said, "How long did you remain on the earth in number of years?" They said, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count."﴾

* * *

As for His saying ﴿بَلاغٌ﴾ [balagh, "a notification"]:

There are two interpretations of it. One is that its meaning is: "They did not remain except an hour of a day; that remaining is a provision (balagh) for them," meaning: that is a provision for them in the world until their term, and then "that remaining" was omitted, while still intended in the speech, being sufficiently indicated by what was mentioned in the speech. The other is that its meaning is: this Qur'an and admonition is a notification (balagh) and a sufficiency for them, if they reflect and take heed and so remember.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿So will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾

Exalted is His remembrance says: So will God destroy by His punishment, when He sends it down, except the people who opposed His command, departed from His obedience, and disbelieved in Him? The meaning of the speech is: God destroys none except the defiantly disobedient people.

It was in a similar manner to what we have said that the people of interpretation spoke.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾: "Know that none is destroyed before God except one who is destroyed, who turns his back to Islam, or a hypocrite who affirms with his tongue and opposes with his deeds." It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: "Whoever among my community intends a good deed, one is written for him; and if he does it, ten of its like are written for him. And whoever intends an evil deed, it is not written against him; and if he does it, one evil deed is written. Then if he follows it, God erases it, and none is destroyed except one who is destroyed."

End of the commentary on Surat al-Ahqaf.
